analyst_view.overall: Early view: Arsenal lead the league with 27 points from 10 games, seven clean sheets and a string of 1-0 wins, including at Anfield. Brentford lost 2-0 at Brighton after Igor Thiago was sent off by VAR for an arm to the face of Chema; a straight red for violent conduct usually brings a three-match ban, which would rule him out of this game, though I did not find the ban confirmed. Bukayo Saka is out with a quad injury, while William Saliba is back in training.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.3 goals. I lean lower: Arsenal have scored only 15 in 10 games and won 1-0 in both of their last two league games, and Brentford are likely without Thiago for this one if the standard three-game ban applies. A low-scoring Arsenal win looks most likely.

corners.text: The site has 9.9 corners. I agree: both sides are dangerous from set pieces and will look to win corners, while Arsenal usually have more of the ball. Nothing in the news moves this far.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.7 cards. I lean higher: Brentford have had two players sent off this season (Yehor Yarmoliuk and Thiago), and Keith Andrews complained that opponents provoked both incidents, which hints at a side that gets drawn into battles. A physical game against the leaders could add bookings.

shots.text: The site has 25.0 shots. I lean lower: Arsenal control games and defend deep when ahead, as they did at Liverpool and Hull, and Brentford without Thiago lose their focal point. Fewer shots than the figure.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 7.2 shots on target. I lean lower: Arsenal did not allow a single shot on target at Anfield, and they missed the target with big chances against Hull, Mikel Arteta said. Six or so on target fits better.
